simple.meaning: לַהַט (lahaṭ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a blaze ; also (from the idea of enwrapping) magic (as covert).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 3:24. The surrounding context includes Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לַהַט (H3858) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: לַהַט (lahaṭ) / H3858 is traced through Genesis 3:24, Exodus 7:11 with generated occurrence evidence.

occurrences.englishText: So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim* cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10. at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.
Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers. They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.
